paper_title: NExtLong Toward Effective Long-Context Training without Long Documents
caption: NExtLong reduces the model's dependence on proximal text. We calculated the degree of dependence on proximal text (the last third of the text) for different methods when completing the LongQA task. It can be observed that NExtLong significantly reduces the model's dependence on proximal text.
model_annotation: This bar chart, titled "Short-Dependence Attention Weight," illustrates the degree of dependence on proximal text—defined as the last third of the input—for five different methods when completing the LongQA task, as presented in the paper "NExtLong Toward Effective Long-Context Training without Long Documents." The vertical axis, labeled "Attention Weight," is scaled linearly from 0.80 to 0.90, with gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 0.02. The horizontal axis, labeled "Methods," lists the five methods in the order: Standard, ICLM, KNN, Quest, and NExtLong. Each method is represented by a single, light blue bar corresponding to its Short-Dependence Attention Weight value. The "Standard" method has the highest attention weight at approximately 0.87, followed closely by "KNN" and "Quest" at approximately 0.865. The "ICLM" method shows a lower weight of approximately 0.85. The "NExtLong" method has the lowest attention weight among the five, at approximately 0.83, visually confirming its ability to reduce dependence on proximal text as stated in the caption. The chart includes a legend indicating that the light blue bars represent "Short-Dependence Attention Weight," and the bars are not sorted, appearing in the order listed on the x-axis.
